children: Australian shares rose on Friday, led by financials and gold miners, as investor sentiment improved after comments from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller eased concerns over further U.S. interest rate hikes.
The S&P/ASX 200 index

was up 0.2% at 9,035.40 points, as at 0050 GMT. The benchmark closed 0.5% higher on Thursday, although the bounce did little to erase the week's losses, leaving the benchmark on track for a weekly decline of around 0.5%.

Expectations of a rate increase shifted slightly this week after second-quarter GDP data bolstered the case for a Reserve Bank of Australia hike at this month's meeting, with investors now pricing in a 67% chance of a September move.

Speaking at a Reuters NEXT Newsmaker event, Waller said that if incoming data confirmed inflation was cooling, he would lean toward supporting a pause in rate hikes at the U.S. Federal Reserve's next meeting.
Back in Sydney markets, financial stocks
rose 0.5%, with the "Big Four" banks gaining between 0.3% and nearly 1%.
Technology stocks
gained 0.8%, tracking overnight gains on Wall Street.
Meanwhile, the broader mining sub-index
slipped 0.3%, dragged down by heavyweights BHP Group
and Rio Tinto
, which fell 1.6% and 0.5%, respectively.
These losses were partly countered by robust gains in gold stocks
, which rose 2.4% on the day, although the sub-index is set to snap a six-week winning streak. Gold prices firmed as expectations for U.S. rate hikes eased.
Energy stocks
dropped 0.6%, with Ampol
falling 6.3%.
New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index
rose 0.6% to 13,937.79 points. Reserve Bank of New Zealand Monetary Policy Committee member Carl Hansen said that this week's rate-hike decision reflected clear consensus among committee members.
